correctness.rationale: From original RESULT.md and verify.py, put x=2^(a-1): sigma-n=(2x-1)(p-1)+6x-2 and phi=x(p-1). Divisibility iff t=(6x-2)/(p-1) is positive integer with t=1 mod x. For a>=2, t odd divides 3x-1, so t is 1,x+1,2x+1; x+1>=5 would divide 4, 2x+1>=9 would divide 5 when x>=4, impossible. Cases x=1,2 yield precisely stated exceptional pairs. For t=1 quotient=2, exception t values give 3 and 4. Independent exact-integer divisibility on 20,876 exponent/prime pairs corroborates but does not prove infinite claim; original algebra does.
